extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO (particularly trademark/non-patent practitioners), respondents in OED disciplinary proceedings, and USPTO enforcement staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing resignation, exclusion on consent, publication, and reinstatement for practitioners before the USPTO, together with the specific USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct provisions cited as alleged violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner status (37 C.F.R. § 11.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is a 'practitioner' pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that persons admitted to practice who appear before the Office are subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's authority to approve resignation and exclude (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32; 37 C.F.R. § 11.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, the USPTO Director has authority to approve an Affidavit of Resignation and to exclude a practitioner on consent from practice before the Office in trademark and other non-patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory and regulatory basis for approving resignation on consent and entering exclusion orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation compliance (37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation must comply with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a) for approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the affidavit satisfies § 11.27(a), the Director may approve it and exclude the practitioner on consent; the Final Order notes approval here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Exclusion on Consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be excluded on consent from practice before the Office in trademark and other non-patent matters commencing on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusion on consent limits the practitioner's ability to practice before the USPTO in the specified subject areas as of the order's effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of disciplinary orders and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's electronic FOIA Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary actions and exclusions on consent are made publicly accessible via OED FOIA Reading Room and Official Gazette notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement presumptions (37 C.F.R. § 11.60 consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: If and when the respondent applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume for purposes of reinstatement that (a) the facts in the OED files are true, and (b) the respondent could not have successfully defended against the allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resignation on consent may trigger conclusive presumptions against the practitioner in future reinstatement proceedings under § 11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates compliance with rules governing resignation and reinstatement procedures and effects.

rubrics_metrics.description: (proscribing other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office)

rubrics_metrics.name: Alleged deficiencies in representation (factual allegations)
rubrics_metrics.description: During representation of trademark clients, respondent allegedly: did not properly communicate with clients; did not properly withdraw from representation; did not act with fairness to opposing parties and counsel; did not exercise diligence and competence; did not pursue clients' objectives; did not consult with clients about means to pursue objectives; did not properly expedite TTAB proceedings; did not give proper access to evidence to opposing parties; did not obey TTAB court orders; did not comply with proper discovery requests; did not properly supervise his staff; made misrepresentations to clients and to the TTAB; and acted in a manner that adversely reflected on his fitness to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factual allegations illustrate the types of conduct that can be found to violate the cited Rules of Professional Conduct and support disciplinary action or exclusion on consent.
